answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent only earns payout weight after completing verifiable tasks on chains like ember logistics grids, tundra data relays, or knoll sensor audits, with registration fees set above the average value of an agent's first month of work. Every fake identity then costs real compute, time, and fees before earning anything, so mass-registration only pays if the work itself is faked, which the task network can detect, making attack cost exceed any payout.
